parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
I often travel abroad with my parents. They're both painters so they really enjoy visiting museums all over the world. Last summer we went to Italy. We visited a lot of beautiful cities but the one I liked best was Florence. The lady who took us sightseeing was my father's art teacher. She's lived in Florence for over 30 years so she knows a lot of interesting facts about the city.

Florence has a lot of things to see. On the first day we went to the Uffizi Museum. There were a lot of beautiful paintings, but I was a bit frightened when I saw Caravaggio's Medusa. This painting shows the head of a woman whose hair is actually snakes! My little brother started crying when he saw it, so we had to leave the room!

We spent the next three days walking around the town. Fortunately, it was sunny all the time, so we visited several wonderful buildings in the city centre and had a nice walk along the Arno river. There are a lot of nice bridges, but one of the oldest ones, Ponte Vecchio, is amazing because it's got real shops on it.

I never thought I would find Florence so interesting. It's a shame we only stayed there for four days, so we weren't able to see that much. However, my parents have decided we'll go back. We're going to spend a few weeks there next time so we'll have time to visit what we missed.

questions.question: Why did Jamal's parents decide to visit Italy?

options.A: They wanted to visit beautiful cities.
options.C: They wanted to see his father's art teacher.

questions.question: Why did Jamal and his family leave the Uffizi Museum?

options.A: Jamal was frightened by a picture.
options.B: There were some snakes in the museum.

questions.question: What did Jamal and his family do in the following days?

options.C: They went sunbathing by the river.

questions.question: Why is Ponte Vecchio so special?

options.B: because it's more beautiful than the other bridges
options.C: because it has buildings on it

questions.question: What does Jamal say about his trip?

options.A: He thought it was a bit boring.
options.B: He is sorry that it was so short.
options.C: He's sad because he misses Florence.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a teacher telling some boys and girls about the school's summer music classes.
parts.transcript:
Good morning class. I'd like to tell you about the music classes that the school is offering this summer. If you're interested in learning to play a musical instrument, you need to book before the 4th July. All the classes will start on the 14th of July and last until the 28th July.
You can choose from several musical instruments such as the drums, the guitar and the violin. Most lessons are on weekdays but the guitar teacher can only teach students on Saturday.
As the courses are all for beginners, you can borrow an instrument from the school. You can collect them from Room 30 on the third floor from the first week of July.
The course isn't very expensive: each of the ten lessons will cost £7, so £70 in total. However, if you pay for the whole course at once, you get a 10% discount and will only pay 63 pounds.

parts.context: You will hear Carol and her friend Richard talk about a film they have seen.

questions.question: What do Carol and Richard both think about the film?
What is Carol doing next?

options.C: She's going to meet her friends.

questions.question: What does Richard think about the length of the film?

options.C: The film wasn't too long or too short.

questions.question: Carol and Richard agree that

options.B: they didn't know anything about the history.

questions.question: Which film are Carol and Richard going to see next time?

parts.transcript:
Carol: How did you like the film?
Richard: Well, I don't usually enjoy watching films about history, I think they're boring. But this time I found it quite interesting.
Carol: I agree with you. I suppose it was because the actors were really good. I loved them, especially the girl playing young Queen Elizabeth.
Richard: I'm not so sure… actually, what I liked best was the photography.
Carol: It was a bit long. I wanted to meet my friends after the movie, but it's already 6 and I have to go home now. I'm going to Cork tomorrow morning.
Richard: But it was only 2 and a half hours long. A film about the life of a queen can't be shorter than that!
Carol: Maybe you're right. At least we've learnt something useful. We're studying the life of Queen Elizabeth at school.
Richard: Yes, it will help us with the history test we've got next week.
Carol: True. So, what about going to the cinema again next Saturday? There's a film about Queen Victoria…
Richard: Well, as I told you, I'm not into historical films. Why not watch a horror or a comedy?
Carol: Horror films are too scary! Let's go see something funny.

parts.title: Listening - Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Antonio talking to his sister about the summer holidays. What did each of his friends do?
parts.transcript:
Sister: How was your first day of school, Antonio?
Antonio: Brilliant. Seeing my classmates again after two months was great fun.
Sister: Did you tell them you went to Austria by train?
Antonio: Yep, and guess what? Oliver went there too but he took the plane.
Sister: Did Megan spend the holidays with her grandparents in France as usual?
Antonio: She did, but she was really bored. She said her parents are planning to go to Portugal or Wales next summer.
Sister: Portugal! I'd love to go there, too. And where did the others go?
Antonio: Michael visited a lot of Irish towns and villages with his aunt.
Sister: And where was Sophie? She is really brown!
Antonio: She was in sunny Spain. Lucky Sophie!
Sister: Did Liam go to Brazil to meet his cousins?
Antonio: No, he'll probably go there at Christmas. He just spent a few weeks in Scotland where his father works.
